name: main: protected
_comment_bypass: RepositoryAdmin can bypass. This is here for one reason: GitHub does not
let anyone approve their own pull request, so on a single-maintainer
repository a code-owner-review requirement would lock the maintainer out
REMOVE THIS ENTRY the moment a second maintainer exists. Until then it is
the difference between a rule and a wall.
Note that the bypass permits the merge, it does not skip the status checks
in the GitHub UI, and an admin merging past a red build is a deliberate,
visible act rather than an accident.

rules._comment: Only code owners can approve, so only code owners can merge.

_comment: The Day 0 gates. A branch cannot merge past a red build, and cannot
merge while behind main with stale passing checks.
'All checks green' is the important one. GitHub only blocks a merge on
checks listed here, so a job that is not listed can fail and be merged
past, and a job added later is not listed by definition. That aggregate
job depends on every other job, runs with if: always(), and fails if any
of them failed. So ANY failing check blocks the merge, required or not.
The individual checks are listed as well, deliberately. If the aggregate
job were renamed or removed, its context would stop reporting and the
hole would reopen quietly. scripts/check-ci-gates.py asserts both that
the aggregate depends on every job and that every job is listed here, and
it runs in the Style job, so this list cannot drift from the workflow.

rules._comment: No force pushing over shared history.
